title: Lifting a morphism between projective resolutions in an abelian category
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let $M,N$ be objects of $\mathcal A$. Let $P_\bullet\xrightarrow{\epsilon_P}M$ and $Q_\bullet\xrightarrow{\epsilon_Q}N$ be augmented nonnegative chain complexes: $d_n:P_n\to P_{n-1}$ for $n\geq1$, with $d_nd_{n+1}=0$ and $\epsilon_Pd_1=0$, and similarly for $Q$. Suppose both augmented sequences are exact (the augmentation is an epimorphism, its kernel is the image of $d_1$, and $\ker d_n=\operatorname{im}d_{n+1}$ for $n\geq1$), and every term is projective, meaning every morphism from that term lifts through every epimorphism in $\mathcal A$. For every morphism $f:M\to N$, there exists a chain map $u:P_\bullet\to Q_\bullet$ with $\epsilon_Qu_0=f\epsilon_P$. No assumption that all objects of $\mathcal A$ admit projective resolutions is made.
